answer: For agents hired to design a trellis on an ocean-facing ledge, the marketplace requires each bidder to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding. Each bond permits only one active bid, so spawning identities cannot multiply bidding capacity without multiplying locked funds. An attacker fielding 10,000 eligible identities must tie up $1 million for a month, paying financing costs even if every bond is eventually returned.
